newsitem.title: CUBA: Two explosions rock central Havana hotels.
newsitem.headline: Two explosions rock central Havana hotels.

text.p: Two loud explosions rocked two central Havana hotels within minutes of each other on Saturday and one witness said it appeared at least three people were hurt.

There was no indication as to what caused the explosions at the Hotel Nacional and the nearby Hotel Capri. A Danish tourist who was sitting in the Hotel Nacional garden at the time of the explosion said he saw at least three people on the ground afterward, apparently injured.

The tourist, Ole Madsen, told Reuters that some of those on the ground at the Nacional were bleeding. He did not know if the injured were Cubans or foreign tourists. At least four ambulances left the hotel about 20 minutes after the explosion, although it was not clear if they carried wounded people.
Witnesses said the explosions took place at about 11:25 a.m. (1525 GMT) and 11:30 a.m. (1530 GMT).

A security cordon of uniformed police and plainclothes security officials prevented reporters entering the Nacional. But Madsen said the explosion there appeared to have ripped through a row of telephone booths in the lobby. He said ground floor windows opening on the hotel's back garden were broken.

About 200 yards (metres) up the street at the Hotel Capri, at least three ground floor front windows were shattered by the explosion there. The explosion also appeared to have hit the lobby, although police prevented reporters from entering.
